source.extracted_fields: catalog metadata only (name, facts, footprint, reference URLs, modelling notes); no model code

use: Scale and proportion targets for asset briefs and review --expect dimensions.
Starting points for research: re-check every figure against the listed references before relying on it.
footprint_m is plan size at heading 0: w along X, l along Z, in metres, as measured on Muster's display models (weapon and gear footprints may include the display stand).
The ps1_ww2_frontline profile requires fictionalized designs without exact branding; use this data for scale, not for replicating a specific real product.

entries.name: Messerschmitt Bf 109 G-6
entries.subtitle: Single-seat fighter, 1943

facts.label: Armament (as modelled)
facts.value: 1 x 20 mm MG 151/20 engine cannon, 2 x 13 mm MG 131

facts.label: Canopy (as modelled)
facts.value: Framed hood with armoured-glass head rest (Galland-Panzer)

entries.modelling_notes: Represents a mid-1943 production G-6 with the standard framed canopy (starboard-hinged hood plus fixed rear glazing) fitted with the armoured-glass head rest known as the Galland-Panzer, the fixed 350 x 135 mm tail wheel and the VDM 9-12087 propeller; no underwing cannon gondolas, drop tank or rack. The swastika normally carried on the fin is deliberately omitted; unit markings, individual numbers, Werknummer and stencils are also left off, so only the Balkenkreuz national markings are shown. Span, length, wing area, propeller diameter and wheel sizes follow the published figures; fuselage sections, MG 131 blisters, supercharger intake, oil cooler, radiators and undercarriage geometry are proportioned from photographs and general drawings rather than factory drawings, and the NACA 2R1 wing sections are approximated by a cambered NACA 4-digit profile. The three-point ground angle is modelled at 12 degrees. The automatic slats are shown dropped open, as commonly seen on parked 109s. The RLM 74/75/76 splinter and side mottle are procedural; panel lines and fasteners are painted rather than modelled, ailerons and flaps are not separated, the engine is not modelled inside the cowling, and the cockpit is simplified (instrument faces are a painted panel; rudder pedals, gun breeches and wiring are omitted).

entries.name: Feldflasche 31
entries.subtitle: M31 canteen with drinking cup
entries.modelling_notes: Bottle and cup maker markings omitted; the screw cap is modelled but hidden under the cup. Harness simplified to one band and one vertical strap with buckle and hook.

entries.name: Entrenching Tool with Bayonet
entries.subtitle: Kleines Schanzzeug and S84/98 III bayonet

facts.label: Carrier
facts.value: Presstoff (pressed board), leather loops and strap

entries.modelling_notes: Carrier maker stampings omitted; the bayonet blade is not modelled (it stays in the scabbard). Frog simplified to sleeve, belt tab and hilt strap.

entries.name: 8.8 cm Flak 36
entries.subtitle: 88 mm heavy anti-aircraft gun
entries.modelling_notes: Represents a Flak 36 in the emplaced firing position in the 1943-44 factory Dunkelgelb finish with moderate wear and no markings: both side outriggers lowered, the four levelling jacks down on their round pads and the two Sonderanhaenger 202 bogies removed. Key numbers: barrel 4.93 m, bore height 1.60 m at 0 degrees, shield 1.95 x 1.75 m with swept 6 mm side plates. The platform arm lengths (about 5.2 x 5.0 m over the pads), the shape of the pedestal, upper carriage, equilibrator cylinders, cradle, fuze-setting machine, data receivers, seats and handwheels are approximated from photographs rather than factory drawings; the barrel section joint is shown as a single collar. Internal mechanisms (recoil brake, recuperator internals, equilibrator springs, gearing, firing gear), the loading tray, cables to the predictor, the travel lock detail, ammunition and crew kit are not modelled.

entries.name: Focke-Wulf Fw 190 A-8
entries.subtitle: Single-seat fighter, 1944

facts.label: Engine
facts.value: BMW 801 D-2 14-cylinder two-row radial, 1,730 PS for take-off

facts.label: Propeller
facts.value: VDM 9-12176 A, three blades, 3.3 m diameter

entries.modelling_notes: Represents a 1944 production Fw 190 A-8 with the standard flat-topped sliding hood (the bulged "blown" hood was only introduced on the line in the last production batches), the pilot head armour inside the hood, four MG 151/20 wing cannon with their wing-root and outer overwing blisters, and the pitot head on the starboard wing tip. The swastika normally carried on the fin is deliberately omitted; unit markings, individual numbers, Werknummer, fuselage bands and stencils are also left off, so only the Balkenkreuz national markings are shown. Span, length, wing area, propeller diameter and track follow the published figures; fuselage sections, cowling, canopy, tail surfaces and undercarriage geometry are proportioned from photographs and general drawings rather than factory drawings, the NACA 230-series sections are approximated by a cambered NACA 4-digit profile and the three-point ground angle (12.5 deg) is an estimate. Simplifications: the ETC 501 fuselage rack, FuG 16ZY and FuG 25a aerials under the fuselage and wing are not fitted; the inner wheel-well doors are shown closed; the engine is represented only by the cooling fan and a dark engine face behind it; flaps and ailerons are not separated; panel lines and fasteners are painted; the RLM 74/75 splinter, RLM 76 undersides and the side mottle are procedural patterns, not the official scheme template; the cockpit is simplified (instrument faces are a painted panel).

entries.name: Kar98k
entries.subtitle: Bolt-action rifle, 7.92 x 57 mm
entries.modelling_notes: Represents a 1940s-production rifle with a solid walnut stock (laminated stocks, introduced from 1937, were more common in mid-war production; walnut continued to be fitted), cupped butt plate, hooded front sight and a leather sling on the left side. Overall and barrel length follow the published figures; stock contours, sight and band positions are proportioned from photographs. Manufacturer codes, proof and acceptance stamps and serial numbers are omitted; the internal mechanism is modelled only where visible.

entries.name: Kubelwagen (Type 82)
entries.subtitle: Light personnel car (4x2)
entries.modelling_notes: Dimensions, tyre size, control layout, door hinging, windscreen, floor gratings and the rear hub reduction follow the US technical manual TM E9-803 (1944); panel curvature, swage positions, lamp and seat details are estimated from photographs. The engine compartment is closed: only the underside of the engine, transaxle, exhaust and suspension is modelled. Generic cross-country tread without sidewall lettering; seat covers shown as cloth (wartime coverings varied); floor pan and running gear shown in dark grey. No registration plates or unit markings; the only markings are the tyre-pressure stencils (1,4 / 1,8 atu). Battery, fuel tank, wiring, cables and side curtains are not modelled.

entries.name: M40 Steel Helmet
entries.subtitle: Stahlhelm M1940 with M31 liner

facts.label: Shell
facts.value: Pressed steel, rolled edge, stamped vents

facts.label: Liner
facts.value: M31, leather on a metal band

entries.modelling_notes: Shell proportions approximated for a size 64 shell fitting a ~56-57 cm head; liner simplified to band, sweatband, nine fingers and drawstring. Maker and size stampings omitted. No decals are shown.

entries.name: MG 42 Gunner (1943-44)
entries.subtitle: German Army infantry, MG 42
entries.modelling_notes: One body type and face, one static pose; cloth folds are procedural. The tool pouch and holster are simplified external shapes (contents not modelled). Weapon and gear pieces are the project's own models (germany/weapons, germany/gear). The national eagle is not depicted.

entries.name: MG 42
entries.subtitle: General-purpose machine gun, 7.92 x 57 mm
entries.modelling_notes: Represents a mid-war MG 42 with a Bakelite butt stock, bipod on the front holder and a 50-round belt drum. Overall and barrel length follow the published figures; receiver, jacket perforations, sights and bipod are proportioned from photographs. The carrying sling is simplified to a single leather strap (the issue sling had two straps and a padded middle section). Markings and the internal mechanism are omitted; the barrel and bolt are modelled only where visible.

entries.name: MP 40
entries.subtitle: Submachine gun, 9 x 19 mm
entries.modelling_notes: Represents a mid-war MP 40: smooth receiver tube, ribbed magazine housing and magazine, two-part bolt handle, hex barrel-collar nut with the strap loop on the right, phenolic resting bar and folded-back 200 m rear-sight leaf. Proportions follow the published overall, folded and barrel lengths; the grip rake, rear-sight and ejection-port positions, slot sizes and sling hardware are close approximations from descriptions, not measured drawings. Grip plates are shown smooth. Maker codes, serial numbers and acceptance stamps are omitted. The internal mechanism is modelled only where visible (bolt, extractor, recoil-spring tube). Shown on the shared display stand.

entries.name: Opel Blitz 3.6-36S
entries.subtitle: 3-tonne cargo truck (4x2)

facts.label: Engine
facts.value: 3,626 cc six-cylinder OHV petrol, 68 hp (military rating)

references: http://www.autogallery.org.ru/blitz36.htm (data after W. Oswald, Kraftfahrzeuge und Panzer der Reichswehr, Wehrmacht und Bundeswehr)
entries.modelling_notes: Length, width, heights, wheelbase, track, ground clearance, platform size and tyre size follow published data; overhangs, cab, bonnet and wing shapes, the bonnet louvre pattern and fitting positions are estimated from photographs of preserved trucks and scale-model references. The all-steel Opel cab is modelled, not the wooden Einheitsfahrerhaus fitted to the Daimler-Benz-built L 701 from late 1944; late details shown are the Notek lamp and the grille without maker's badge. Dunkelgelb applies from the 1943 colour order; the frame and running gear are shown in black-grey (factory practice varied). The spare wheel is shown carried under the rear frame overhang and the fuel tank under the seat; exact positions varied with body type and are simplified. The engine is represented by its underside masses only; wiring, brake lines and cables are omitted. Generic cross-country tread; olive-khaki tarpaulin. No registration plates, unit or tactical markings.

entries.name: 7.5 cm PaK 40
entries.subtitle: 75 mm anti-tank gun
entries.modelling_notes: Represents a 1943-44 gun in factory Dunkelgelb with moderate wear and no markings, fitted with the early full-disc pressed-steel wheels with an impressed spoke pattern (the later spoked wheels are not modelled). Key numbers: barrel 3.45 m, firing height 0.96 m, wheel diameter ~0.9 m, track ~1.6 m, trail spread ~3.6 m. Hand-wheel, gearbox, sight-bracket, shutter and spade shapes are approximated from photographs rather than factory drawings; internal mechanisms (buffer, recuperator, torsion bars, semi-automatic and firing gear) are not modelled. The barrel is shown at 0 degrees elevation and traverse. Closed shows the unhitched travel layout: trails brought together with the towing eye between their ends, spades folded and the lower-shield flap raised, the trail ends resting on the ground (the gun tips back slightly). The barrel travel lock, the third wheel for manhandling, ammunition and crew kit are omitted.

entries.name: Panther Ausf. G
entries.subtitle: Medium tank (Pz.Kpfw. V, Sd.Kfz. 171)
entries.modelling_notes: Depicts a late Ausf. G (autumn 1944 onwards) with the chin mantlet, the rotating driver's periscope, the bow MG ball mount, rubber-tyred 860 mm road wheels and plain exhaust pipes in cast guards (no flame dampers), no Zimmerit. Plate layout, heights, the station spacing and fitting positions were derived from published overall dimensions, armour data and photographs, not from factory drawings; the drive sprocket and idler are shown narrower than the real parts so that they run clear of the interleaved wheels. Left and right wheel stations are symmetric (the real torsion bars stagger them). Hatches are closed and no interior is modelled; tool stowage is representative and simplified, the cupola AA MG and the antenna rods are not fitted. Markings are limited to Balkenkreuze (no unit or turret numbers). The optional three-tone scheme is a generic sprayed Olivgruen / Rotbraun pattern over Dunkelgelb, not the pattern of one documented vehicle.

entries.name: Panzer IV Ausf. H
entries.subtitle: Medium tank (Pz.Kpfw. IV, Sd.Kfz. 161/2)
entries.modelling_notes: Depicts early (mid-1943) production: rubber-tyred return rollers, tubular idler, no Zimmerit, no turret smoke dischargers, single Bosch headlight on the left track guard, antenna base on the rear deck with the rod antenna not fitted, deflector rod under the gun. Plate layout was derived from published overall dimensions and photographs, not factory drawings. Hatches are closed and no interior is modelled. Tool stowage, belly covers, bin and bracket details are representative and simplified; the cupola MG ring is shown without its MG 34. Markings are limited to Balkenkreuze (no unit or turret numbers).

entries.name: Rifleman (1943-44)
entries.subtitle: German Army infantry, Kar98k
entries.modelling_notes: One body type and face, one static pose; cloth folds are procedural. The belt kit follows the standard 1939 arrangement in simplified form (e.g. the gas-mask sling routing and the assault-pack bag contents are generalised). The Y-straps pass under the tunic shoulder straps. Weapon and gear pieces are the project's own models (germany/weapons, germany/gear). The national eagle is not depicted on the cap or tunic.

entries.name: Squad Leader (1943-44)
entries.subtitle: German Army infantry, MP 40
entries.modelling_notes: One body type and face, one static pose; cloth folds are procedural. The belt kit follows the standard 1939 arrangement in simplified form; items often carried by NCOs (binoculars, map case, whistle) are omitted. Weapon and gear pieces are the project's own models (germany/weapons, germany/gear). The national eagle is not depicted.

entries.name: Stielhandgranate 24
entries.subtitle: Model 24 stick grenade
entries.modelling_notes: Exterior only; stencilled instructions and maker stampings are omitted. No fragmentation sleeve fitted.

entries.name: StuG III Ausf. G
entries.subtitle: Assault gun (Sturmgeschuetz III, Sd.Kfz. 142/1)
entries.modelling_notes: Depicts mid-1943 production: welded box mantlet (Kastenblende; the cast Topfblende or "Saukopf" mantlet followed from November 1943), single-piece 80 mm nose plate, no smoke dischargers and no Zimmerit. Plate layout and component positions were derived from published overall dimensions and photographs, not factory drawings; the casemate is simplified (no bolted add-on plates, simplified pannier construction). Hatches are closed and no interior is modelled. The loader's MG 34 is simplified; the stated 2.16 m height excludes the raised MG shield. Tool stowage, spare wheel and spare link positions are representative. Antenna base only, rod not fitted. Markings are limited to Balkenkreuze (no unit numbers).

entries.name: Tiger I Ausf. E
entries.subtitle: Heavy tank (Pz.Kpfw. VI, Sd.Kfz. 181)

facts.label: Width
facts.value: 3.55 m on combat tracks (3.14 m on transport tracks)

entries.modelling_notes: Depicts a mid-production Tiger I as completed in about July 1943: second-pattern turret with the low cast cupola (seven periscopes, AA MG ring), escape hatch for the loader, simplified pistol-port plug and the loader periscope, twin Bosch headlights (the right one was deleted from August 1943), five S-mine launchers, oval Feifel air pre-cleaners, guarded exhaust mufflers, rubber-tyred road wheels with 12-bolt rims, no smoke dischargers (deleted June 1943) and no Zimmerit (factory application began in the late summer of 1943; sources give dates from July to September). Plate layout, turret proportions and fitting positions were derived from published overall dimensions, armour data and photographs, not from factory drawings. The wheel interleaving follows published descriptions (three wheels per arm, the outermost wheel on the outer track extension); left and right stations are shown symmetric, whereas the real torsion bars stagger them slightly. Hatches are closed and no interior is modelled. Tool and cable stowage, the spare links on the turret sides and the engine-deck details are representative of 1943 vehicles rather than one specific tank; the deep-wading equipment, the antenna rod and the cupola MG 34 are not fitted. Markings are limited to Balkenkreuze (no unit or turret numbers).

entries.name: Carro Armato M13/40
entries.subtitle: Medium tank

facts.label: Machine guns
facts.value: 8 mm Breda Mod. 38: co-axial, twin hull mount, plus one anti-aircraft

facts.label: Armour
facts.value: 30 mm hull front, 25 mm sides, 42 mm gun mantlet

facts.label: Suspension
facts.value: Leaf-sprung bogies, 8 double road wheels per side; 26 cm tracks

facts.label: Produced
facts.value: Ansaldo-Fossati, 1940-41; 710 per Italian sources (other totals up to about 780)

entries.modelling_notes: Depicts a III serie tank (short front mudguards, tool boxes and silencers on the rear mudguards, one spare road wheel and the jack on the rear plate, roof bulge over the breech). Overall dimensions follow the published 4.915 x 2.28 x 2.37 m; plate junction heights, bogie spacing and fitting positions are proportioned from photographs, not factory drawings. The track has 80 links per side (regioesercito.it; other sources give 84). Hatches are closed and no interior is modelled; the radio mast is shown lowered and the anti-aircraft Breda is not fitted. Markings follow the 1940 Regio Esercito tactical system (company rectangle, platoon bars, vehicle number); the number plate is left blank.

entries.name: Arisaka Type 99
entries.subtitle: Bolt-action short rifle, 7.7x58mm
entries.modelling_notes: Represents an early / mid-war Type 99 short rifle: blued metal, two-piece stock with the lower butt piece spliced on horizontally, cupped steel butt plate, side-mounted (left) sling swivels, reinforced upper band with the bayonet lug, front sight protectors, ladder rear sight with the anti-aircraft lead arms shown folded, straight bolt handle with the plum-shaped knob, knurled safety knob, optional sliding dust cover and a brown leather sling. Overall and barrel length follow published figures; the stock sections, receiver, sights, bands and swivels are proportioned from photographs, not measured. The folding monopod of early rifles is not fitted (it was frequently removed). The receiver ring is shown plain: the imperial chrysanthemum and all other markings are deliberately omitted. Bolt shown closed; internal mechanism, the Type 30 bayonet and the sling stitching / buckle tongue are not modelled; the sling adjustment is a simplification.

entries.name: Type 97 Chi-Ha
entries.subtitle: Medium tank (57 mm gun)

facts.label: Machine guns
facts.value: 2 x 7.7 mm Type 97 (hull front left, turret rear)

facts.label: Engine
facts.value: Mitsubishi SA12200VD air-cooled V-12 diesel, 170 hp

facts.label: Suspension
facts.value: Bell crank, 6 road wheels per side; 96 links per track

entries.modelling_notes: Overall dimensions, crew, armament, suspension layout (six double road wheels, the centre four in two bogies, three return rollers, front sprocket, rear idler, 96 single-horn links) follow the references; the nose plates are modelled a little steeper than the published 80 / 62 degrees so the nose closes over the final drives; plate junction heights, the turret plan, fitting positions and the tool stowage are proportioned from photographs and published drawings, not factory drawings. The layout of the exhaust silencers and tools follows common photographs rather than one specific vehicle. Paint is the 1942 three-colour scheme (parched-grass khaki base with dark green and mahogany brown patches, no yellow stripe); unit markings are omitted. Hatches are closed and no interior is modelled.

entries.name: Type 99 Light Machine Gun
entries.subtitle: Light machine gun, 7.7x58mm
entries.modelling_notes: Represents an early-production gun with the folding monopod under the butt (shown folded), blued metal, a wooden butt with a black-finished steel butt plate, a grooved wooden pistol grip, a canvas sling and open sights offset to the left of the magazine. Overall and barrel length follow published figures; receiver, butt, grip, magazine curvature, barrel fins, carrying handle, gas system, bipod and sight positions are proportioned from photographs and descriptions, not measured. The carrying handle is shown folded to the right; the side-opening magazine-well cover is shown open. Sling swivel positions and hardware, bipod leg length and foot shape are approximations. Receiver markings (arsenal insignia, dates, serials), the telescopic sight rail and the internal mechanism are not depicted; the bayonet is not modelled.

entries.name: Glass Water Flask
entries.subtitle: 0.75 l flask in cloth cover

facts.label: Closure
facts.value: Rubber plug tied to the neck with a cord

facts.label: Cover
facts.value: Cloth bag with drawstring and shoulder strap

entries.modelling_notes: Exact flask dimensions were not found; body size (about 131 x 67 x 190 mm with the neck) is estimated from the 0.75 l capacity and period photographs. Cover patterns varied widely; a simple two-panel drawstring bag with a sewn-on cotton strap is shown. The glass body itself is hidden by the cover; only the neck and plug are modelled in detail.

entries.name: DP-27
entries.subtitle: Light machine gun, 7.62 x 54 mmR

facts.label: Action
facts.value: Gas-operated, automatic fire only, open bolt

facts.label: Sights
facts.value: Sector rear sight to 1,500 m; post front sight with protective ears

entries.modelling_notes: Proportions from the published overall and barrel lengths and scaled side-view photographs (265 mm pan). Layout after the manual: casing of two joined tubes (barrel tube with windows, guide tube below), front sight with protective ears on the casing front, sector rear sight on the receiver behind the pan, bipod collar with wing screw, sling swivels on the casing and on the left of the butt. Internal mechanism (bolt, locking flaps, recoil spring) is not modelled; the stamped pattern of the pan cover, the sling hardware and the rear-sight scale are approximations. No factory markings or serial numbers.

entries.name: F-1 Hand Grenade
entries.subtitle: Defensive fragmentation grenade
entries.modelling_notes: Fuze internals are not modelled; the lever, pin and ring follow the UZRG layout in simplified form. Block count of the body grooving is approximate.

entries.name: GAZ-67B
entries.subtitle: Light 4x4 field car
entries.modelling_notes: Length, width, wheelbase (2.10 m, confirmed by several sources), track, overhangs and tyre size follow published data; body heights, panel shapes and fitting positions are estimated from photographs of preserved vehicles. Engine, gearbox and transfer case are simplified blocks under the bonnet and floor; the differentials are shown on the centre line and the exhaust routing is simplified. Wiring, brake cables and fuel lines are omitted. Seat pads are shown as dark leatherette; the canvas top is shown folded and strapped at the rear. No markings are applied.

entries.name: Ilyushin Il-2
entries.subtitle: Two-seat ground-attack aircraft, 1943-44

facts.label: Armament (as fitted)
facts.value: 2 x 23 mm VYa-23 cannon, 2 x 7.62 mm ShKAS (wings); 1 x 12.7 mm UBT (rear)

entries.modelling_notes: Span, length, wing area, centre-section chord, tailplane span, 15 deg outer-panel sweep, wheel sizes and the 3.6 m propeller follow the sources; fuselage cross-sections, wing thickness, gear track (~3.4 m) and the three-point ground angle (~10 deg) are estimates from photographs, not measured drawings. Shown as a 1943-44 aircraft with wooden rear fuselage, VYa-23 cannon, UBT on its pivot mount and no external stores; RS-82 rails, antenna, pitot, trim tabs and most rivet/fastener detail are omitted. Radiator and oil-cooler intake shapes are simplified. The camouflage is a generic sprayed AMT-4/AMT-6 pattern over AMT-7, not a copy of a specific factory template; markings are red stars with white border and thin red outline, no unit numbers. Cockpit interior is simplified (panel, sight, seat, stick, head armour, gunner strap seat).

entries.name: IS-2 Model 1944
entries.subtitle: Heavy tank

facts.label: Machine guns
facts.value: 3 x 7.62 mm DT (coaxial, fixed bow, turret rear); 12.7 mm DShK AA from 1945

facts.label: Armour
facts.value: Upper glacis 120 mm at 60 deg; turret front 100 mm

entries.modelling_notes: Exterior only, hatches closed, no crew or interior. The cast turret is a smooth signed-distance approximation proportioned from a scale drawing and photographs; casting numbers and foundry marks are omitted, and the gun embrasure behind the bent-plate mantlet is simplified. Weld beads and plate joints are idealised and the belly seams are not modelled. Running gear follows the published figures (six dual 550 mm road wheels, three return rollers, rear sprocket with two 14-tooth rings, 86 single-horn 650 mm links per side), with simplified castings. Stowage (ZIP box, tow cable, shovel, crowbar, spare links, four 90-litre external tanks) follows late-war photographs; exact positions are estimated. The fixed bow DT port is shown (the bow gun was later deleted; sources give no date), and the DShK mount is simplified. No markings, since tactical numbers and slogans varied by unit. Model length is 9.83 m; the top of the cupola hatch is at 2.77 m (2.63-2.73 m quoted).

entries.name: KV-1 Model 1941
entries.subtitle: Heavy tank, welded turret

facts.label: Main gun
facts.value: 76.2 mm ZiS-5 (41.6 calibres), fitted from autumn 1941

facts.label: Machine guns
facts.value: 3 x 7.62 mm DT (coaxial, bow, turret rear)

facts.label: Armour
facts.value: Hull front 75 mm; 25-35 mm applique plates added in 1941

facts.label: Suspension
facts.value: Torsion bars, six road wheels and three return rollers per side; 700 mm tracks

entries.modelling_notes: Exterior only, hatches closed, no crew or interior. Overall dimensions (hull 6.675 m, width 3.32 m, height 2.71 m, 0.45 m clearance), the running-gear layout (six dual 600 mm road wheels, three rubber-tyred return rollers, rear sprocket, 700 mm single-horn links on a 160 mm pitch) and the ZiS-5 barrel length follow published figures; plate angles and junction heights, the turret plan and all fitting positions are estimated from photographs. The length with the gun forward (about 7.2 m) follows from the barrel length and is not a published figure. The welded turret is idealised (flat plates, simplified mantlet and vision devices); the road wheels are the 1941 ribbed rubber-tyred pattern, simplified. Stowage (five 160-litre tanks, ZIP boxes, tow cable, shovel, crowbar) follows descriptions of late-1941 Chelyabinsk tanks; exact positions are estimated. No markings, since tactical numbers and slogans varied by unit.

entries.name: DP-27 Gunner (1943-44)
entries.subtitle: Red Army infantry, DP-27 light machine gun
entries.modelling_notes: Figure, uniform and kit are simplified: one body type and face, one static pose; cloth folds are procedural. Weapon and gear pieces are the project's own models (soviet/weapons, soviet/gear).

entries.name: Mosin-Nagant M1891/30
entries.subtitle: Bolt-action rifle, 7.62 x 54 mmR

facts.label: Sights
facts.value: Hooded post; tangent rear sight, 100-2,000 m

entries.modelling_notes: Represents a wartime round-receiver M1891/30 with a birch stock, straight bolt handle and canvas sling on leather dog collars. Overall, barrel and bayonet lengths follow the references; stock profile heights and the exact sight, band and slot geometry are close approximations from photographs. The sling slots are shown as escutcheon-lined openings rather than fully cut through the stock. Arsenal stamps, serial numbers and the internal mechanism (firing pin, interrupter, extractor) are omitted.

entries.name: MPL-50 Infantry Shovel
entries.subtitle: Small entrenching tool with canvas cover
entries.modelling_notes: Blade outline, socket straps and cover are simplified from photographs; cover closure is shown as a strap with a wire buckle. Weight is not stated because published figures vary between variants.

entries.name: PPSh-41
entries.subtitle: Submachine gun, 7.62 x 25 mm Tokarev

facts.label: Weight
facts.value: 3.63 kg empty; 5.45 kg with a loaded drum

facts.label: Sights
facts.value: Hooded post; L-type flip rear sight, 100 / 200 m

The drum and box magazine are shown closed (no internal spiral or cartridges); the bolt is visible through the ejection port and handle slot, other internals are omitted. Markings are omitted.

entries.name: Rifleman (1943-44)
entries.subtitle: Red Army infantry, Mosin-Nagant M1891/30
entries.modelling_notes: Figure, uniform and kit are simplified: one body type and face, one static pose; cloth folds are procedural. Weapon and gear pieces are the project's own models (soviet/weapons, soviet/gear).

entries.name: SSh-40 Steel Helmet
entries.subtitle: Infantry steel helmet

facts.label: Liner
facts.value: Three pads, six rivets, drawstring adjustment

references: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He%C5%82m_wz._50 (post-war Polish copy, used for shell proportions ~271 x 248 x 166 mm)
entries.modelling_notes: Shell proportions follow the published dimensions of the closely derived Polish wz. 50; exact SSh-40 size-2 dimensions were not found. Liner pads are simplified (no internal felt or size markings).

entries.name: SU-76M
entries.subtitle: Light self-propelled gun

facts.label: Engines
facts.value: Two GAZ-202 six-cylinder petrol engines, 2 x 70 hp

facts.label: Armour
facts.value: 25-35 mm front, 10-15 mm sides; open-topped casemate

facts.label: Suspension
facts.value: Torsion bars, six road wheels and three return rollers per side

entries.modelling_notes: Overall dimensions (about 5.0 x 2.74 x 2.14 m, 0.30 m clearance), the plate angles (upper front 60 deg, lower front 30 deg, casemate front 25 deg, casemate sides about 20 deg), the running-gear layout (six 550 mm road wheels on torsion bars, three return rollers, front sprocket, rear idler of the road-wheel pattern, 300 mm small-link tracks) and the ZiS-3 ordnance follow published figures; plate junction heights, the casemate plan and all fitting positions are estimated from photographs. The engines and fuel tanks are internal and not modelled; their layout (engines in line on the right, fuel tanks on the left of the driver) is shown only through the roof fittings (engine hatch, radiator grille and outlet louvre on the right, filler caps on the left) and the twin exhaust mufflers on the right track guard, whose exact positions are approximate. The gun mount, moving shield and armoured recoil-gear cover are simplified; the interior is simplified (pedestal, hand wheels, sight, seats, part of the 60-round load in racks, stowed DT machine gun) and the driver's compartment is not modelled. entries.modelling_notes: Exterior only, hatches closed, no crew or interior. Weld beads and plate joints are idealised. Stowage follows the 1944 Factory No. 183 layout described in the references (one 90-litre tank on the left and two on the right at the stern, large ZIP box, tow-cable lugs, headlight and horn on the left, small ZIP box and spare-link bosses on the right), but exact positions are estimated; the two-man saw, tarpaulin and smoke canisters are omitted and the tow cable is shown as a single length. Road wheels are the partially ribbed rubber-tyred type; tracks are 72 cast 500 mm links per side, alternating horned and flat. No markings, since tactical numbers and slogans varied by unit. Overall model length is 8.16 m against the 8.1-8.15 m quoted in sources.

entries.name: ZiS-5V

entries.modelling_notes: Length, width, height, wheelbase, track, clearance, platform size and loading height, spring lengths and leaf counts and tyre size follow published data; overhangs, cab, bonnet and wing shapes and fitting positions are estimated from photographs of preserved trucks. entries.modelling_notes: Represents a 1944 LF Mk IXc with the "C" wing: one Hispano in the inner cannon bay of each wing, the unused outer cannon position closed by a short plugged stub, two .303 Browning ports per wing and the small teardrop feed blisters; standard elliptical wing tips (not clipped), the standard rounded rudder (the later broad-chord pointed rudder is not fitted), the fixed tail wheel, six fishtail exhaust stacks per side and the temperate (non-Aero-Vee) carburettor intake. Span, length, wing area, dihedral, washout, propeller diameter and track follow the published figures; fuselage sections, canopy, radiator housings and gear geometry are proportioned from photographs and a Mk Vb general-arrangement drawing (nose lengthened for the Merlin 66), not from factory drawings, and the three-point ground angle (11.5 deg) is an estimate. Panel lines are painted rather than modelled; ailerons, flaps, gun-bay doors and the cockpit access door are indicated by panel lines only; the engine is not modelled under the cowling; the cockpit is simplified (dials are rings on a plain panel; rudder pedals, oxygen and wiring are omitted); IFF aerials and landing lamps are omitted.

entries.name: BAR M1918A2

Dimensions of the individual parts are proportioned from those, not measured. The hinged shoulder rest is shown folded. Omitted: the butt monopod (dropped from production in 1942) and the barrel carrying handle (a late-war addition); the action is shown closed, internal parts, the rate reducer in the butt, receiver markings and serial numbers are not modelled.

facts.label: Finish (as modelled)
facts.value: Natural metal, aluminium-lacquered wings, olive drab anti-glare panel

entries.modelling_notes: Represents a P-51D-20-NA (straight dorsal fin fillet, K-14 gunsight, no rocket stubs) in late-1944 factory finish: bare aluminium fuselage and tail, wings filled and painted with aluminium lacquer, bare flaps, ailerons and gun-bay doors, olive drab anti-glare panel, black propeller blades with yellow tips. Only the national star-and-bar insignia are applied; unit codes, serials, nose art, stencils and squadron colours are deliberately omitted. Span, length, wing area, propeller diameter and the published parked height (4.08 m, tail down, one blade vertical) set the proportions and the ~10 deg three-point attitude; the wing uses the published P-51D root and tip ordinates, but fuselage sections, scoops, canopy, tail and undercarriage geometry are proportioned from photographs and general drawings, not factory drawings. The inner main-gear doors are shown drooped open as often seen on parked aircraft. Panel lines and fasteners are painted, not modelled; the engine is not modelled inside the cowling; the cockpit is simplified (painted instrument faces; no wiring, pedals or oxygen system).

entries.name: Thompson M1A1
entries.subtitle: Submachine gun, .45 ACP
entries.modelling_notes: Represents a wartime M1A1 with Parkerized metal, walnut butt stock, pistol grip and horizontal fore-grip, a blued 30-round (or 20-round) box magazine and an olive-drab web sling on the US-pattern swivels under the fore-grip and under the butt. Overall and barrel length follow the published figures; receiver, frame, grip, stock and sights are proportioned from those and from parts descriptions (side cocking handle on the right, selector and safety levers on the left, fixed peep sight with protective wings). The action is shown closed (bolt forward); internal parts, markings and serial numbers are not modelled. On the display stand the sling is laid to the viewer side of the cradles.

facts.value: 1.77 m top up, 1.32 m top down

entries.modelling_notes: Wheelbase, length, width, heights, tread, ground clearance, tyre and wheel size, spring lengths and leaf counts follow TM 9-803 (1944); windscreen pane size follows reproduction glass data. Body heights, overhangs, panel shapes and fitting positions are estimated from photographs of preserved vehicles. Lamp layout follows TM 9-803 and parts references (sealed-beam headlamps behind the grille, blackout marker lamps on the grille below them, hooded blackout driving lamp on the left fender, combination tail lamps); the axe and shovel sit on the body left side, the fuel can at the rear left and the spare wheel at the rear right as listed for WWII vehicles, but their exact brackets are simplified. The engine compartment is closed: only the radiator, the underside of the engine, gearbox, transfer case, propeller shafts and exhaust are modelled. The steering-wheel spoke pattern, instrument layout and data plates are approximated; the non-directional tread is a simplified bar pattern without sidewall lettering. Wiring, brake and fuel lines, the fuel tank under the driver seat and the side curtains are not modelled. The canvas top is shown folded and strapped on the folded bows. The only marking is the optional white hood star; registration numbers and unit markings are omitted.
